statement: Theorem 3.2 gives the Bellman equation for the integrated Q function of the lifted mean-field control problem.
conditions: Paper's finite state/action MFC lift and discounted objective.
limits: The action is a population-level local-control distribution, not a raw joint action.

statement: Theorem 5.5 proves Algorithm 4.1 converges linearly to the approximate fixed point and bounds its sup-norm error from the true Q by terms proportional to discretization scale ε.
limits: The constants include kernel/net geometry and sampled-model errors.

statement: Theorem 5.6 bounds the time needed for an ε-greedy exploration policy to visit all ε-net neighborhoods under the reachability assumption.
conditions: Assumption 5.1 and the theorem's exploration and confidence parameters.
limits: The covering bound can be large in state/action dimension despite independence from N.

statement: Theorem 6.3 bounds the cooperative finite-N value difference from its MFC counterpart by C/√N under interchangeability, Lipschitz-policy, and contraction assumptions.
limits: Not an O(1/N) rate and not arbitrary heterogeneous MARL.

statement: Traffic experiments report MFC-K-Q outperforming tested MARL baselines for large N, including the paper's N>50 regime.
conditions: Network congestion simulator, paper hyperparameters, and separately evaluated sizes.
limits: Does not identify one frozen policy tested on a held-out roster.

statement: N-independent mean-field learning complexity plus O(N^{-1/2}) approximation must not be read as generic held-out-N policy robustness.
conditions: Bounded to the formal decomposition in this work.
limits: A new shared-policy experiment could test transfer.

statement: HMASD could use population-measure state and kernel Bellman updates as a transparent variable-roster planning baseline before moving to deep continuous control.
conditions: Requires population observability, continuous-state adaptation, and one-policy cross-N evaluation.
